Eligible studies were randomized trials with an average of at least 100 participants per arm.

canonical_statement: Eligible interventions included any NSAID, any opioid, and any preparation of acetaminophen or paracetamol.
The protocol specified acetaminophen or paracetamol and placebo as comparators.

The prespecified primary outcome was pain, selected through a hierarchy that prioritized global pain, walking pain, WOMAC pain, other composite pain measures, activity pain, global indexes, and global assessments.
Pain data were planned for 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, and 48 weeks, or end of treatment when not covered by a prespecified time point.
Physical function was the prespecified secondary efficacy outcome and used a parallel hierarchy of function scales.

Safety outcomes included lack of efficacy, any dropout, any adverse event, serious adverse events, dropout due to adverse events, and all-cause mortality; adverse events were analyzed as binary outcomes.
The search strategy included CENTRAL, reference lists of retrieved articles and reviews, and ClinicalTrials.gov.
Two review authors independently assessed potentially eligible titles and abstracts, with disagreements resolved by consensus or a third investigator.

For multiple reports of one trial, the protocol prioritized the most comprehensive information, regulatory information over peer-reviewed information, peer-reviewed information over non-peer-reviewed information, and newer information over older information.
Data extraction covered trial design, sample size, follow-up duration, dose, treatment duration, participant characteristics, index joint, outcome type, and outcome data at each time point.

For crossover trials, data before crossover were extracted to avoid carryover, graph-derived approximations were permitted when necessary, and intention-to-treat results were preferred when available.
Risk-of-bias assessment covered random sequence generation, allocation concealment, patient blinding, and adequacy of analysis, with intention-to-treat analysis used as the adequacy criterion.
Continuous outcomes were modeled as standardized mean differences and binary outcomes as odds ratios.
The efficacy synthesis used an extension of multivariable Bayesian random-effects models for mixed multiple-treatment comparisons.
The longitudinal model used a random walk so outcomes at adjacent time points within a trial were modeled as more similar than outcomes at more distant time points.

The protocol specified a gamma prior for between-trial heterogeneity and a uniform prior for between-timepoint heterogeneity, with a half-normal between-trial heterogeneity prior used in sensitivity analysis.
Model fit assessment used standardized node residuals, Q-Q plots, posterior between-trial variance, and comparison of direct and indirect treatment effects.
The minimum clinically important between-group difference was set at 0.37 standardized-deviation units, corresponding to 9 mm on a 100 mm visual analog scale.
Analyses were planned in Stata and OpenBUGS.
The primary outcome was adjusted for trial characteristics through meta-regression, and separate analyses by time point were planned to assess variation over time.
The protocol states that the Arthritis Society of Canada grant YIO-17-0164 had no role in study design, data collection, synthesis, interpretation, report writing, or submission decisions.
The protocol states that none of the authors was affiliated with or funded by a manufacturer of an evaluated agent.
